text: Prince Lothric and Prince Lorian, though expected to sacrifice themselves to link the First Flame, refused to do so, choosing to let the Age of Fire die rather than sacrifice themselves for a few more years, and retreated to the highest chamber of Lothric Castle, triggering the crisis.
Lothric's refusal to link the fire caused the First Flame to begin fading rapidly.
In response to Lothric and Lorian's joint refusal to link the flame, the emergency bells tolled, summoning the old Lords of Cinder from their graves instead of new champions.

After being resurrected, most of the Lords of Cinder remembered the pain of linking the fire and refused to return to their thrones; of the four raised, all except Lothric of Carim abandoned their thrones and refused to link the flame again.
The player's character is an Unkindled who rises from a grave in the Cemetery of Ash at the start of the game.
Four Lords of Cinder rose from death: Lothric of Carim, Aldrich Saint of the Deep, the Abyss Watchers, and Yhorm the Giant.
When even the proven Lords of Cinder refused to link the flame, the bells tolled once more, summoning the Unkindled, failed undead champions who had never become proper cinder.
Iudex Gundyr was once a champion who sought to link the fire but arrived too late, as it had already been linked by another.
Vordt of the Boreal Valley was once an Outrider Knight of Irithyll serving under Pontiff Sulyvahn.
The Evangelists send captured undead from the Undead Settlement to the Cathedral of the Deep as food for Aldrich.
The Road of Sacrifices was historically used to march condemned undead to the Cathedral of the Deep as food for Aldrich.

The Cathedral of the Deep was formerly a holy site of the Way of White religion; its priests originally performed holy rites and used flame to seal and purify the corruption known as the Deep before eventually succumbing to its influence.
The Deep gradually corrupted the clergy of the Cathedral, who abandoned the Way of White and began worshipping the darkness instead.
Aldrich was interred within the Cathedral of the Deep before becoming a Lord of Cinder, and his presence there accelerated the Deep's corruption and transformation of the clergy.
The priests who tended Aldrich's resting place began venerating him as the Saint of the Deep.
By the time Aldrich rose and left for Irithyll, the Cathedral of the Deep had already fully fallen to corruption.
Aldrich's coffin behind the altar of the Cathedral of the Deep is found empty, since he departed for Irithyll immediately after rising.
The Cathedral of the Deep imprisoned Aldrich but could not execute him due to his immense power, so they forced him to become a Lord of Cinder as a means of control.
Before becoming a Lord of Cinder, Aldrich was a cleric with an uncontrollable hunger for human flesh, and Pontiff Sulyvahn exiled him to the Cathedral of the Deep to contain the problem.
The Abyss Watchers partook of the wolf essence of Artorias, an ancient knight who had battled the abyss long ago, binding them into sharing a single soul.
The Abyss Watchers linked the First Flame together as one legion, their combined strength sufficient to kindle it, becoming Lords of Cinder through their shared soul.
After linking the flame, the Abyss Watchers' shared essence began to dry up and the abyss started corrupting their fortress and ranks; consumed by infighting, they forgot their duty afterward.
When the Abyss Watchers were resurrected by the tolling bell, some had resisted abyssal corruption while others succumbed, leading the order into civil war with itself.
The catacombs of Carthus lie beneath Farron Keep and are the remains of the fallen kingdom of Carthus, once famous for warriors and pyromancers.
Highlord Wolnir was once the conqueror of Carthus who sought more power from the Abyss, which slowly consumed him.
Irithyll of the Boreal Valley was once protected by the old gods ruling from Anor Londo, with Gwyndolin as the last active deity maintaining order.

Pontiff Sulyvahn weakened and imprisoned Gwyndolin by unclear means, removing the last obstacle to his rule, then declared himself Pontiff of Irithyll, holding Gwyndolin captive in the Cathedral of Anor Londo.

After Aldrich was resurrected as a Lord of Cinder and returned with greater power, Pontiff Sulyvahn, rather than opposing him, facilitated his march on Irithyll and capture of Anor Londo, striking a deal to offer him the imprisoned Gwyndolin to feast on in exchange for leaving Irithyll alone.
After the emergency bell tolled, Aldrich journeyed to Anor Londo to consume the imprisoned god Gwyndolin, slowly devouring him over what must have been an agonizing period.
Anor Londo was once the legendary city of the gods where Lord Gwyn ruled during the Age of Fire, but the gods have long since abandoned it.
While burning within the first flame after being forced to link it, Aldrich experienced visions of an age of the deep sea and decided to embrace the Deep as its champion.
After defeating Aldrich, two Lords of Cinder (the Abyss Watchers and Aldrich) have fallen, leaving Yhorm the Giant and Prince Lothric unaccounted for.
The cinders of a lord found within Aldrich's remains proved he had once linked the first flame.
After three Lords of Cinder (Abyss Watchers, Aldrich, Yhorm) were defeated, only Prince Lothric remained unaccounted for.
Yhorm the Giant was descended from an ancient conqueror whose lineage predated the current crisis by generations.
A curse combined with the interference of unscrupulous court sorcerers caused the eruption of the Profaned Flame in Yhorm's capital.
The Profaned Flame destroyed every human being in the Profaned Capital, while Yhorm the Giant survived because giants were hardier than humans.
In grief over his people's destruction, Yhorm the Giant chose to link the first flame, hoping the power gained would protect his people and subdue the Profaned Flame.
Yhorm the Giant became a Lord of Cinder by linking the first flame, but the Profaned Flame continued to rain down and devastate his capital regardless, destroying his people anyway.
When the Lords of Cinder were resurrected by the tolling of the emergency bell, Yhorm the Giant returned to find his capital unchanged, still in ruins.
The Dancer of the Boreal Valley was, like Vordt, once an Irithyllian Outrider Knight of old royal lineage before being transformed by Sulyvahn's cursed eye rings.
Lorian willingly took on part of Prince Lothric's curse to share his burden, losing his own legs and voice as the price.
An unnamed mentor encouraged Prince Lothric to question the necessity of the endless cycle of sacrifice, fueling his decision to reject the flame.
The kingdom of Lothric was built around a prophecy and generations of bloodline management meant to produce a prince who would link the flame.
The Ashen One claims the cinders of Lothric, completing the set of four hunted Lords of Cinder: the Abyss Watchers, Aldrich, Yhorm, and Lothric.
Ludleth of Courland had linked the first flame once before of his own free will, prior to the events of the game.

The Kiln of the First Flame is the original place where Lord Gwyn first became a Lord of Cinder, sacrificing himself by splitting his Lord Soul among trusted servants and Seath before walking into the dying flame as kindling.
Gael asks the Ashen One to enter the painting and reignite flame in the Painted World of Ariandel, a world that has forgotten fire, hoping two bearers of ash fulfill a prophecy of renewal.
Sister Frieda convinced Father Ariandel to use a bowl of his own blood to suppress the cleansing flame, allowing the painted world to rot rather than be renewed.
Slave Knight Gael continues his search for the Dark Soul of Man pigment beyond the painting, eventually traveling to the Ringed City.
Gael's mission was to find the Pygmy Lords and claim the Dark Soul within them to bring its pigment to the Painter so she could create a new world.
Because the Pygmy Lords' blood had dried into dust, Gael slaughtered them and devoured their dried blood in an attempt to extract the Dark Soul's pigment.

Lord Gwyn sent those whose dark souls he feared most—the Pygmy Lords, descendants of the Furtive Pygmy who claimed the Dark Soul at the dawn of disparity—to the Ringed City, which he built to serve as both prison and sanctuary.

Gwyn sent his youngest daughter Filianore to the Ringed City to watch over the Pygmies, a gesture that primarily served to keep the darkness locked away; she held a mysterious egg whose seal kept the Ringed City separate from the rest of the world, guarded by the Ringed Knights.
The four Lord Soul-bearers waged war against the everlasting dragons, with Gwyn using lightning to shear stone scales from the dragons.
The Witch of Izalith used firestorms and Nito unleashed death itself against the dragons during the war.
Seath the Scaleless, a dragon born without scales and an outcast among his kind, betrayed the dragons by teaching the gods how to kill immortal dragons.
The gods won the war against the dragons, ending the Age of Ancients and beginning the Age of Fire.
The Four Kings of New Londo received a fragment of Gwyn's Lord Soul for building a great underground civilization, a gift that later caused their downfall when the Abyss consumed New Londo.
Gwyn's sacrifice in linking the First Flame created the Dark Sign, a curse marking certain humans as undead who resurrect at bonfires after death instead of dying permanently.
Afflicted undead were gathered and locked away in remote asylums by the gods, who feared them.
In Drangleic, King Vendrick sought to break the curse of the undead and end the cycle, but failed and eventually went hollow, wandering his own kingdom's crypts.
Lorian's greatest triumph was defeating the Demon Prince, one of the last remnants of the chaos demons born from the Witch of Izalith's failed attempt to recreate the first flame.
Gwyn's firstborn son was a god of war who fought alongside Gwyn against the everlasting dragons, wielding lightning spears capable of piercing dragon scales.

Gwyn's firstborn son was exiled, stripped of his deific status, and had his name erased from all records after betraying Gwyn by allying with the everlasting dragons, becoming known only as the Nameless King.
After his exile, the Nameless King allied with storm drakes, descendants of the ancient dragons, and tamed one known as the King of the Storm.
